newsitem.title: USA: U.S. attracts more foreign crudes, Latam trade up.
newsitem.headline: U.S. attracts more foreign crudes, Latam trade up.

text.p: U.S. foreign crude markets stayed relatively subdued ahead of the weekend, although more sellers were sighted offering delivered cargoes.
North Sea Brent was offered at Dec West Texas Intermediate +20 cents cif for late Nov arrival, and Cano Limon was asked around WTI -$1.40/1.50 fob for late Dec.
The transAtlantic arbitrage, still holding narrowly at 60 cents for Dec, kept demand buoyant for foreign barrels while also injecting fresh momentum into grades.
"The drop in Dated Brent should encourange traders to move more supplies to the U.S.," an East Coast trader said.
In nearby markets, Ecopetrol sold one Vasconia cargo at less than $2 discount to WTI fob Colombia, to a U.S. refiner, traders said.
Cano Limon for Dec 4-8 was believed sold to another U.S. refiner, but the price was not immediately available.
Two traders were seen holding Cusiana stems for December, with prices notionally around Jan WTI +30-35 cents fob.
Additionally, Oriente was nominally at $2.90 discount to WTI, traders said.
In the U.S. aftermarket, three full boats traded for Dec, once at $23.20, and twice at $23.30 a barrel, about 30 cents above the London IPE close.
Brent intermonth Dec/Jan traded at 40 cents, up from about 30 cents during the London market.
